definition: Optimization involving objective functions with multiple local minima, saddle points, or other complexities, lacking the strong theoretical guarantees of convex optimization.
details: Deep neural network training is a canonical example of non-convex optimization, yet empirically, techniques like SGD and its variants have proven remarkably effective at finding good solutions despite the lack of theoretical convergence guarantees.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Non-Convex Optimization.
